what: Invitation Homes owns about 80,000 single-family rental houses across the American Sun Belt and rents them to families who want a house with a yard rather than an apartment.
customers: Households in Atlanta, Dallas, Phoenix, Tampa, Orlando and other southern metros, on one-year leases.
money: monthly rent on the owned portfolio
managing houses owned by joint ventures and third parties
moat: Scale in a business that is otherwise owned by individuals: thousands of houses in the same metros make maintenance crews, leasing and pricing cheaper per house than any small landlord can manage.
risks: High mortgage rates keep people renting, but they also raise the cost of buying more houses
Several states and cities have proposed rules limiting institutional ownership of single-family homes
$8.4B of debt against $130M of cash, so refinancing terms matter a great deal
opportunities: Free cash flow of $950M against a $15.0B market value, and analysts see about 25% upside
A 21.5% net margin, high for a landlord, because scale keeps the cost of running each house down
Houses are expensive to buy and mortgages are dear, which keeps the pool of renters large
watch: Same-home rent growth and the share of houses occupied.
